View All /Calendar.aspx OverviewTo ensure you receive timely alerts and warnings during emergencies, we recommend you sign up for Sarpy County ALERTS, get a NOAA Weather Radio All Hazards (NWR), and familiarize yourself with the outdoor warning siren system, Wireless Emergency Alerts (WEA), and the Emergency Alert System (EAS). See the following sections to learn more about Sarpy County ALERTS and the outdoor warning siren system. To learn about Wireless Emergency Alerts (WEAs), the Emergency Alert System (EAS), and NOAA Weather Radio All Hazards (NWR) visit www.ready.gov/alerts.We have a limited number of NOAA Weather Radios available to residents at no cost. Priority is given to households with vulnerable individuals, including those experiencing financial hardship. Click here to request a radio.Sarpy County ALERTSSarpy County ALERTS (powered by AlertSense/Konexus) is a free service, provided by the Sarpy County Emergency Management Agency, that sends emergency alerts, warnings, and other public safety related information to subscribers via email, text messages, voice calls, and push notifications through mobile applications. Click on the buttons below to sign up to receive alerts, modify a current subscription or unsubscribe, and to download the myAlerts app from Google Play or the App Store. Outdoor Warning Siren SystemThe outdoor warning sirens are activated when a potentially life-threatening hazard is possible, imminent, or occurring.When the sirens sound, take shelter immediately and then seek emergency information from a trusted source such as the National Weather Service via NOAA Weather Radio or local media.The sirens sound for three minutes per activation and may activate multiple times over the course of a warning.Depending on the situation, siren activation may be localized to the warned area or encompass the entire county.There is no "all-clear" siren. The sirens should not be relied upon to give sufficient warning indoors or in noisy areas.Siren TestsTests of the outdoor warning siren system are regularly conducted to help maintain the integrity of the system.Monthly tests of the system (including all sirens) are conducted on the first Wednesday of every month at 11 a.m. A scheduled test may be canceled if severe weather is possible or if temperatures are forecast to be at or below freezing.Brief tests (less than 30 seconds) of individual sirens are occasionally conducted (typically during servicing).Although the sirens are not tested during the annual Statewide Tornado Drill, we encourage all communities to participate in the drill to practice severe weather plans.Siren ReportsPlease report siren issues by sending an email to ema@sarpy.gov. Please include a detailed description of the issue and the siren number which can be found using the map below (zoom in to see the siren numbers).Siren Location
